original_question: If the notions of positive tree and the principles P^+, P, and P^- are redefined by replacing measure with dimension, what analogs of the measure-based results and separations continue to hold?
target_in_paper: Section 5 (Wei Wang), Problem 11, the question about 'using dimension' immediately after the definitions of positive tree and the principles P^+, P, and P^- and after Problem 10. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2507.03972))
correct_elements: Your draft is pointed at the right place in the paper: it correctly identifies that the target is the dimension-analogue question for the positive-tree principles in Section 5, and it correctly frames the issue as asking which of the nearby measure-based facts and separations should survive after replacing measure by dimension. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2507.03972))
missing_details: The ambient objects are binary trees T ⊆ 2^{<ω} and their path sets [T] ⊆ 2^ω; your draft does not state this setting. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2507.03972))

The paper’s Section 5 defines 'positive tree' in terms of positive measure of [T]; a stand-alone dimension version must say exactly what replaces this, i.e. which notion of dimension is intended on Cantor space. Problem 11 itself leaves 'dimension' implicit. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2507.03972))

The three principles need to be written out explicitly, not only named: P^+ = every positive tree has a perfect positive subtree; P = every positive tree has a perfect subtree; P^- = every positive tree has an infinite countable family of paths. Your draft assumes this notation but does not define it. The exact P^- wording is suppressed in the arXiv HTML extraction, but it is the standard wording of the same hierarchy in the adjacent literature. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2507.03972))

The comparison class in the paper is not a generic body of 'measure-based results' but the specific reverse-mathematical facts listed just before Problems 10 and 11: WKL_0 ⊢ P^+, RCA_0 ⊢ P^+ → P → P^- → 1-RAN ↔ WWKL_0, together with the nonimplications P^+ ⊬ WKL_0, RCA_0 ⊬ P → P^+, and RCA_0 ⊬ 1-RAN → P^-. ([tianyuan.amss.ac.cn](https://tianyuan.amss.ac.cn/upload/fab78d36-bd52-42eb-84d3-ff99c953bb08/20250708/67111751937959724.pdf?utm_source=openai))

The base theory over which these implications and separations are being asked about is RCA_0; your draft does not mention this. ([tianyuan.amss.ac.cn](https://tianyuan.amss.ac.cn/upload/fab78d36-bd52-42eb-84d3-ff99c953bb08/20250708/67111751937959724.pdf?utm_source=openai))

To be fully paper-faithful, the dimension question should also acknowledge the immediately preceding Problem 10, since Problem 11 follows it directly; in particular, one natural part of the dimension analogue is whether the counterpart of P^- → P holds. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2507.03972))
refined_question: Over RCA_0, let T ⊆ 2^{<ω} be a binary tree and [T] ⊆ 2^ω its path set. If one redefines 'positive' to mean that [T] has positive Hausdorff dimension (in the usual Cantor-space metric), and correspondingly defines P^+_dim, P_dim, and P^-_dim by replacing 'positive measure' with 'positive dimension' in the Section 5 principles—namely, P^+_dim: every positive-dimension tree has a perfect subtree of positive dimension; P_dim: every positive-dimension tree has a perfect subtree; and P^-_dim: every positive-dimension tree has an infinite countable family of paths—which of the Section 5 measure-based implications and nonimplications continue to hold for these dimension analogues, and in particular does the analogue of Problem 10, RCA_0 ⊢ P^-_dim → P_dim, hold? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2507.03972))
justification: The draft is clearly targeting Problem 11 rather than Problem 10, because Problem 11 is exactly the paper’s one-line prompt to replace measure by dimension for the positive-tree principles in Section 5. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2507.03972)) Since the official formulation is extremely compressed, the only way to make it stand-alone without broadening it is to import the exact Section 5 setup: binary trees in 2^{<ω}, the three principles P^+, P, P^-, and the specific implication/nonimplication picture displayed immediately beforehand. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2507.03972)) The paper itself does not say which notion of dimension is meant, so the refined question fixes the narrowest standard choice—Hausdorff dimension of [T] in Cantor space—while otherwise staying as close as possible to the paper’s actual intent. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2507.03972))
